title: AI Scientist
description:
ABOUT LENDABLE

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

- One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

- Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

- Profitable since 2017

- Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

- Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/lendable.co.uk)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

JOIN US IF YOU WANT TO

1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

This role combines applied AI engineering, process design and hands-on Python development. You will work on loosely defined problems, test ideas quickly and turn the strongest ones into reliable services.

In under a year, we built a chatbot across Loans, Credit Cards and Motor Finance that now handles more than 1 million customer chats a year at around a 70% resolution rate. It completes complex account actions autonomously, end to end, and we hold it to the same standard as our best operations agents.

We have also built AI document parsers that process around 500,000 documents a year, and are trialling voice AI on our phone lines. You will help take these systems further and find the next high-impact processes to automate.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Improve the chatbot's quality and expand the account actions it can complete autonomously.

- Expand our in-house document extraction pipelines to make parsing faster and more accurate.

- Design LLM-driven workflows that simplify case management.

- Find new opportunities to replace manual work with effective AI systems.

- Own solutions from discovery and prototyping through deployment, evaluation and monitoring.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

- Strong engineering skills and experience building production systems.

- Hands-on experience using LLMs in real workflows.

- Experience designing and improving prompts, retrieval pipelines, agent workflows and evaluations.

- An understanding of business processes and good judgement about where AI can simplify or automate them.

- The ability to structure ambiguous problems, test hypotheses and make progress with partial information.

- Clear communication and the ability to explain trade-offs and influence stakeholders.

WHY JOIN US

- Work with LLMs, retrieval systems, agents and automation pipelines every day.

- Join a small, autonomous team with meaningful ownership and decision-making power.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

1. Introductory call

2. Take-home exercise

3. Take home debrief

4. Case study

5. Onsite final interview

LIFE AT LENDABLE

- Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

- Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

- Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

- Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbe

The Supply Chain Program Manager is a critical cross-functional role responsible for owning end-to-end supply chain execution across assigned programs and product builds at Wayve, including prototype development, new product introduction (NPI), and fleet launches.

You’ll serve as the primary Supply Chain lead for your programs, ensuring program deliverables, supplier compliance and seamless coordination across Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing and external partners. - Identifying long-lead items and critical-path components early in the product lifecycle, tracking material status throughout build phases and proactively escalating gaps and risks.

- Collaborating with Supply Chain Team Leads to ensure direct purchasing, indirect purchasing and logistics suppliers meet legal, environmental, regulatory and ethical sourcing requirements, including TISAX and ISO standards.

- Partnering with Legal and Compliance to ensure appropriate supplier agreements, NDAs and risk controls are in place.

- Developing contingency plans for supply disruptions and actively managing supply chain risks.

- Serving as the primary program manager for upfitter and partner relationships, maintaining stakeholder alignment and driving activities against vehicle timelines and quality standards.

- Proactively identifying and resolving issues affecting vehicle build readiness while coordinating internal teams and external partners.

- Maintaining clear communication cadences with upfitters and stakeholders, tracking milestones and escalating risks as needed.

- Defining, tracking and reporting supply chain KPIs, including material availability, total cost savings and inventory cycle count accuracy.

- Establishing program-level dashboards and reporting cadences that provide leadership and cross-functional stakeholders with visibility into performance.

- Analysing KPI trends to identify root causes of underperformance and drive corrective actions with suppliers and internal teams.

- Using KPI insights to continuously improve supply chain proces

The Home Health and Hospice Coding Specialist is responsible for reviewing clinical documentation and assigning accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for home health and hospice patients. This contractor supports coding accuracy, regulatory compliance, reimbursement integrity, and quality outcomes by ensuring documentation supports the patient’s diagnoses, plan of care, level of service, and Medicare requirements. This role requires strong knowledge of home health and hospice coding guidelines, Medicare Conditions of Participation, LCD/NCD guidance, PDGM requirements, hospice eligibility documentation, and appropriate sequencing of diagnoses.
What You’ll Do In This Role

• Review home health and hospice clinical documentation across all time points (SOC, ROC, Recertification, Transfer, Discharge, Admission) to assign accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes.

• Sequence diagnoses in strict compliance with ICD-10-CM guidelines, CMS requirements, PDGM payment methodologies, and hospice coding expectations.

• Audit clinical charts to identify documentation gaps or inconsistencies, and collaborate with clinical leadership or compliance teams to resolve query needs.

• Support revenue cycle efficiency by meeting established productivity and turnaround time goals to prevent delays in billing and claim submissions.

• Assist with internal quality assurance and external medical reviews, including TPE, ADRs, and compliance audits.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with clinical, QA, compliance, and revenue cycle teams to drive documentation integrity and regulatory readiness.

• Maintain an advanced, current knowledge base of CMS guidance, Medicare regulations, LCDs, and payer-specific updates.

• Ensure absolute data privacy and HIPAA compliance when handling all Protected Health Information (PHI).

• Generate and maintain tracking logs, status updates, and coding reports for management as required.

You will be Cartesia's technical and programmatic owner for SI delivery, responsible for partner readiness, certification standards, implementation quality, and the commercial model that lets the program scale responsibly.

- Build the SI operating model: define partner segmentation, certification tiers, service packages, implementation methodology, scope boundaries, escalation paths, and quality standards.

- Exceptional communication and relationship management skills, with the confidence to challenge partners and internal stakeholders when delivery readiness falls short.

- Technical fluency to lead credible conversations about integrations, configuration, data migration, and implementation design, with sound judgment on when to engage specialists.

- Strong commercial judgment to design partner packages, incentives, payout structures, and guardrails that protect customer outcomes and program economics.

- Operational program design skills (e.g. certification design, scope control, delivery QA, escalation governance, QBRs, playbooks).

- A builder mentality. You're comfortable building 0-to-1 operating mechanisms and shaping foundational systems for long-term success.

title: Maintenance Controller
description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service - spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack - from the lab to the field - we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

Air Mobility Group (AIRMOB) is responsible for developing and delivering Metrea’s aerial refueling (AAR) capabilities, ensuring the readiness and operational effectiveness of the tanker fleet. AIRMOB oversees fleet management, maintenance, and airworthiness, working to sustain and enhance refueling operations. It manages the integration of new processes and technologies, ensuring that tanker aircraft remain mission-ready through effective logistics, maintenance oversight, and regulatory compliance. By coordinating across various teams, AIRMOB ensures the fleet meets both current and future operational needs, supporting a range of specialized air mobility missions. 

Position Summary

The Maintenance Controller is responsible for coordinating and planning maintenance activities on their assigned shift for MSM's KC-135 fleet. This role ensures efficient execution of maintenance operations, provides technical support to maintenance activities, and maintains effective communication between Maintenance, Operations, and Logistics Departments. The position requires technical expertise in aviation maintenance and the ability to ensure compliance with FAA regulations and company policies while reporting directly to the Maintenance Control Manager. 

What You'll Do

• Coordinate and plan maintenance activities and provide technical support on assigned shift 

• Coordinate maintenance activities conducted by Contract Agencies, where applicable

• Ensure contracted maintenance personnel are properly briefed and understand the nature of problems to be worked, as well as company policies and procedures for maintenance activities

• Ensure all work is performed in accordance with current FARs, company manuals, and other Technical Data acceptable to the Administrator

• Provide technical assistance to all maintenance activities and personnel

• Monitor all DMIs (Deferred Maintenance Items) to ensure time limits are not exceeded

• Monitor, update, and verify aircraft status; report aircraft status changes as they occur to Operations and Maintenance

• Execute planning and scheduling of airframe and line engine maintenance/inspections, airworthiness directives, service bulletins, corrosion program requirements, scheduled modifications, and mandatory replacement items as directed

• Assemble Aircraft Maintenance/Insp

Wir begleiten Mediziner:innen durch ihre Promotion - von Methodik über Auswertung bis zur fertigen Dissertation. Unsere Klient:innen sind keine Studenten, sondern erwachsene Profis, die liefern müssen. Du bist die Person, die dafür sorgt, dass das passiert.

Wir sind ein kleines Unternehmen mit hoher Schlagzahl und hoher Effizienz. Wir brauchen sorgfältige, einsatzbereite und belastbare Leute, die methodisch sauber arbeiten, überdurchschnittlich verdienen wollen und in einem wachsenden Unternehmen von Anfang an dabei sein wollen.

• Bodenständigkeit. Du hast in deinem Leben schon einmal richtig gearbeitet - Gastro, Bau, Pflege, Pflichtdienst, Lager, Versorgerjobs, körperliche Tätigkeiten neben dem Studium. Wer einmal eine 10-Stunden-Schicht in der Küche oder auf der Baustelle gemacht hat, weiß, was ehrliche Arbeit bedeutet

About Tiko
Tiko is a high-growth, award-winning African nonprofit on a mission to radically transform healthcare access. Recognized as an Audacious Project awardee and one of the fastest-growing NGOs in the sector, we are committed to strengthening the potential and resilience of adolescent girls across Africa. We address the “Triple Threat” of unintended pregnancy, HIV infection, and sexual and gender-based violence by building local health ecosystems that provide stigma-free, no-cost, quality-assured services.
Our model brings together key local actors: community-based organizations (CBO) with peer mobilisers who act as health companions to girls; public and private health clinics that deliver care; and retail partners that redeem Tiko Miles -our behavior-change incentive programme that rewards service uptake and feedback.
We invest in partners by strengthening CBO capacity, training frontline workers and providers, supporting clinic quality improvement, and compensating partners based on performance. Our technology platform connects all actors by enabling referrals, verifying service delivery, facilitating payments, and generating real-time data.

We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!
Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.

What you will do

Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.
Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.
Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.

Natera is seeking an experienced Clinical Oncology Specialist (COS) to join our specialized Genitourinary (GU) Oncology sales team. This high-impact, tumor-specific role will focus on driving adoption and growth of  Signatera™, Natera's personalized, tumor-informed molecular residual disease (MRD) test , across the GU Oncology landscape.

Entrupy is a global technology company whose mission is to protect businesses, borders and consumers from transacting in counterfeit goods. Entrupy has developed a patented technology system which utilizes a combination of AI and computer vision to instantly identify and authenticate high value physical goods.

Entrupy ’s solutions serve business customers including leading luxury brands, retailers, e-commerce marketplaces and online resellers in over 60 countries. Entrupy is growing quickly with team members based in the US, India, Japan and Brazil. Entrupy ’s solutions in market:

● Entrupy Apparel Authentication

● Entrupy Bags & Leather Goods Authentication

● Entrupy Sneaker Authentication

● Entrupy Fingerprinting

As we continue to build...

We’re seeking curious, growth minded thinkers to help shape our vision, structures and systems; playing a key-role as we launch into our ambitious future. If you’re invigorated by our mission, values, and drive to change the world - we’d love to have you apply.

About the Role
As we expand branded luxury jewelry as a key category, we’re looking for a domain expert to help scale and strengthen our authentication capabilities globally, with a focus on North America.
We already have an established foundation in APAC, and this role will be critical in building depth, consistency, and regional expertise in North America, while partnering closely with the existing team. You will focus exclusively on high-end, branded jewelry (e.g., Cartier, Tiffany, Van Cleef & Arpels, etc.), bringing deep expertise in brand-specific construction, hallmarks, and authentication nuances.
If you are passionate about luxury craftsmanship, brand heritage, and scaling expertise across regions, this is a unique opportunity to play a pivotal role in a growing category.
Reports to Manager, Apparel
Location: US
Employment Type: Remote

• Scale and enhance branded jewelry authentication capabilities in partnership with the APAC team

• Authenticate high-value branded jewelry pieces, contributing to critical, high-risk evaluations

• Build and refine structured knowledge systems (brand-level taxonomies, hallmark libraries, construction guides)

• Develop and localize training programs and certification materials for global teams

• Research luxury jewelry brands, collections, and brand-specific identifiers to deepen category expertise

• Support the expansion of luxury apparel expertise in North America, ensuring consistency in authentication quality

• Coach and mentor team members to foster a high-precision, knowledge-first culture

What you bring:

• 3 to 5+ years of experience in branded luxury jewelry authentication, resale, or appraisal

• Deep expertise in brand-specific hallmarks, engravings, construction techniques, and identifiers (e.g., Cartier, Tiffany, Van Cleef & Arpels, Bulgari, etc.)

• Strong understanding of luxury jewelry brand portfolios, collections, and market positioning

• Experience building training materials, playbooks, or structured knowledge systems

• Exceptional attention to detail and ability to make high-stakes authentication decisions

• Strong communication skills - able to codify expert judgment into scalable processes

• Highly organized, proactive, and comfortable working cross-functionally in a global environment

• Passion for authenticity, craftsmanship, and scaling expertise in luxury categories

But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?   Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.   Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.   Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.   We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY. title: Sr. People Operations Generalist
description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Sr. People Generalist builds the operational backbone of the People team: the processes, systems, data, and policies that let us scale without adding complexity. This is a builder role, not an administrator role. You will turn work that runs on tribal knowledge and one-off fixes into documented, measured, repeatable programs with clear owners and controls.

You will be helping define the center of excellence model on the People team: the escalation point for employee matters, a data connoisseur that owns data fidelity , and the person who decides where work should live as the team matures from reactive support to a proactive shared-services model. You will lead cross-functional projects and use AI to shape the employee experience.

 

AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

- Define the People Ops operating model: what is standardized and centralized, what stays with People Partners or other COEs, and how work transitions with continuity and measurement built in

- Assess the maturity of each core People process (onboarding, offboarding, job changes, comp cycles, leaves, time off, rotations) and run a roadmap to move each from ad hoc to documented, measured, and automated

- Be the operational partner to People Business Partners: execute reorgs, promotions, performance actions, and exits they drive; supply the data and process support behind their work

- Set standards for process design, documentation, SLAs, and handoffs; own the SOP library and knowledge base so answers live in a system

- Support the build of audit-ready controls (recurring data audits, approval trails, segregation of duties) for SOX

- Define service-quality metrics (ticket volume, resolution time, error rate, employee satisfaction) and use them to decide what to fix next

- Run proactive audits across Workday and connected systems to catch errors before they reach payroll, equity, or board reporting

- Serve as a functional Workday owner: business process design from requirements through configuration, testing, and post-launch iteration

- Use AI and low-code tools to prototype and ship People Ops automations; know when a gap needs a lightweight internal tool versus a technical build with IT or Systems

- Resolve the hardest cases in benefits, leaves, time off, rotations, and sensitive org changes with precision, empathy, and clear written communication

- Partner with Finance, Legal, IT, Recruiting, and Payroll on projects that mature processes and policies for the business

- Lead change management for process redesigns and new tools: communication, training, adoption tracking, and feedback

title: Staff Security Analyst (Governance and Trust)
description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. 

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role in a nutshell:

Chainguard is building the secure foundation for software development and deployment. Our Governance & Trust team makes sure the security practices behind that mission are effective, measurable, and worthy of our customers' trust.

We're hiring a senior practitioner to lead the compliance and trust side of that team. You'll run the execution of our external examinations (SOC 2, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials, and a growing set of sector and regional certifications), own how we respond to customer security diligence, and run third-party risk operations. You'll lead the compliance and trust side of the team, which includes a public-sector compliance analyst and two customer-facing security analysts, with formal management of that group expected as the team grows.

This is not a checklist compliance role. Our operating model treats policies and controls as code, draws evidence from systems of record rather than screenshots, and uses AI agents for first-pass questionnaire responses and vendor triage. You'll be the person who decides what those systems need to produce, judges whether what they produce is right, and stands behind it with an auditor or a customer.

What you’ll do:

• Run the execution of Chainguard's external examinations end to end: the evidence calendar, population and completeness-and-accuracy requests, sample fulfilment, auditor status calls, and readiness assessment ahead of each cycle. Work with the Head of Governance & Trust on scope, control applicability, and auditor negotiation.

• Build and keep the working relationships with People, IT, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and Sales that evidence, populations, and remediation depend on. Compliance and trust at Chainguard runs across most of the company, and the function should not be chasing other teams for what it needs.

• Own customer security diligence: security questionnaires, customer audits, Trust Center content, and the multi-round assessments that regulated customers run. Set turnaround expectations with Sales that the team can meet, and decide what we will and won't provide.

• Own the third-party risk management program: vendor intake and tiering, assessments, dispositions, and the register of critical suppliers and their agreements.

• Act as product owner for the customer-facing side of our agent platform: define what the questionnaire responder and vendor triage agents must do, maintain the validated answer bank they draw on, and judge whether their output is good enough to send. Stay current on how other companies handle diligence and response automation, and bring in better approaches when they exist.

• Turn recurring patterns across questionnaires, audits, and vendor reviews into standing artifacts, self-serve packages, and control improvements, so the same question is answered once.

• Work from a single unified controls catalog across frameworks, and push mapping and implementation defects back to the governance side rather than maintaining framework-specific lists.

• Produce findings and remediation evidence that survive external re-test, and feed the corrective-action process with root causes rather than symptoms.

• Guide the public-sector compliance analyst's work on assessor relationships and customer-facing federal diligence, with technical scoping decisions staying with the Head of Gove

title: Senior Engineer- Agentic Development

The Opportunity

FICO builds the analytics and decisioning technology behind some of the highest-stakes decisions in the world economy including the FICO Score, the standard measure of consumer credit risk in the US, and FICO Platform, an API-first applied intelligence platform delivering real-time decisions across fraud detection, credit risk, regulatory compliance, marketing, and customer engagement. This is mission-critical, low-latency, heavily regulated software where auditability and controlled change are non-negotiable. This role sits at the point where that technology is being built and operated in an agentic-first way. As coding agents take on an increasing share of the software lifecycle, the engineer's role shifts from hand-writing code to directing, specifying, and verifying the output of a fleet of specialised agents, working through a structured harness of guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that transforms raw model capability into production grade engineering. The successful candidate will bring the engineering judgement that agents cannot replicate: the ability to define what good looks like, encode it with sufficient precision for agents to achieve it, and recognise when they have not, applying that judgement to architecture, correctness, trade-off analysis, and the design of the work itself.

What You’ll Contribute

• Collaborate with Product teams to translate early stage ideation into structured Proof of Concepts, establishing clear technical feasibility and scope.

• Produce detailed specifications and acceptance criteria that enable coding agents to generate correct, maintainable, and well-architected output, taking full ownership of the resulting code through to deployment.

• Apply rigorous quality standards to all agent generated output, ensuring it meets the same level of scrutiny as hand written code within a regulated decisioning context.

• Operate effectively within the agentic harness, utilising established guides, including AGENTS.md files, architectural rules, and reference documentation alongside automated sensors such as linters, fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers.

• Identify the root cause of recurring agent errors and work with the harness team to implement systemic controls, ensuring the same class of failure cannot recur across the codebase.

• Maintain the accuracy and currency of repository documentation, specifications, and contextual knowledge, treating these as a shared system of record for both human engineers and agents.

• Apply focused technical judgement to architecture decisions, edge case analysis, latency and integration risk, auditability requirements, and any determination that falls outside the appropriate scope of agent autonomy.

What We’re Seeking

• Demonstrable experience in software engineering within large, complex codebases, with a strong foundation in software architecture, testing practices, and long-term maintainability.

• Practical experience working with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or Cursor with a clear understanding of their capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use within a production engineering workflow.

• The technical judgement to critically evaluate agent generated output, identify subtle errors or architectural weaknesses, and make informed decisions about when to intervene in the agent workflow.

• The ability to communicate technical requirements with precision, producing specifications and definitions of done that are unambiguous, testable, and actionable by both agents and engineering colleagues.

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

You will work across the full development lifecycle, from writing and verifying HDL code to developing software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing, integrating embedded software and electronics, and establishing robust development and deployment pipelines.

You will also help establish Proxima’s FPGA development capability beyond plasma heating, defining reusable architectures, development workflows, testing methodologies, and HDL best practices that can be adopted across other systems.

- Design, implement, and maintain HDL-based control and protection systems, starting with plasma heating system protection.

- Collaborate across RF, controls, electronics, and systems teams to define system interfaces, ICDs, and verification plans.

- Strong proficiency in HDL (VHDL, Verilog, SystemVerilog) and software scripting (Python, C/C++).

- Proven experience integrating FPGAs with hardware peripherals, board-level electronics, and communication interfaces.

- Familiarity with modern software development practices (Git, CI, code review, automated testing).

- Systems-thinking approach with strong debugging skills spanning HDL, embedded firmware, and physical hardware.

- High-speed digital interfaces (multi-gigabit serial links, LVDS, SerDes, RF/instrumentation links) and PCB-level signal integrity.

- FPGA+processor platforms and MPSoCs (e.g., AMD/Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+).

- Precision timing and synchronization (IEEE 1588 PTP, White Rabbit)

title: Co-Op, Bayesian Methods for Complex Decision Making
locationText: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences builds AI systems that accelerate discovery across the physical and life sciences. Within Physical Sciences AI, we work with experimental teams to build autonomous discovery agents that decide which experiments Lila's AI Science Factories should run next.

Real scientific campaigns rarely look like textbook optimization problems. A single campaign can mix large discrete choices (which components, which recipe) with continuous settings (amounts, temperatures, times), pursue several objectives under hard constraints, and draw on evidence from literature and characterization data. Every experiment costs real time and materials. Off-the-shelf methods often struggle here, and they ignore the domain structure that could guide the search.

As a Bayesian Methods Co-Op, you will work alongside research scientists and engineers on a focused project within one broad question: how AI systems can make better experimental decisions. Depending on your background, that could mean building agents that choose the next experiment, testing when in-context learners can be trusted as decision-makers, or developing Bayesian strategies for tight experimental budgets. Your methods will be tested against live campaigns.

What You'll Be Building

• Design and benchmark experiment-selection strategies that balance exploration and exploitation under realistic budgets

• Build autonomous discovery agents that propose the next experiment from surrogate models

• Develop in-context learning approaches inspired by Bayesian inference, evaluating calibration and robustness

• Run retrospective and live evaluations on active campaign data with clear baselines and metrics

• Present findings to ML and experimental teams, with the option to contribute to a publication

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Pursuing a Master's or PhD in statistics, ML, CS, operations research, applied math, or a quantitative science

• Solid grounding in Bayesian inference and decision making, including priors and posterior predictive distributions

• Research experience in Gaussian processes, Bayesian optimization, bandits, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modeling

• Strong Python skills with PyTorch and probabilistic libraries such as Pyro, PyMC, or BoTorch

• Comfort working with small, noisy, and heterogeneous datasets

• Clear communication with both ML and experimental collaborators

Bonus Points For

• Applying these methods to real problems in materials science, chemistry, or another physical science

• Familiarity with in-context learning as implicit Bayesian inference, meta-learning, or prior-data fitted networks

• Optimization over categorical or combinatorial spaces, including mixed-variable, multi-objective, or batch settings

• Reinforcement learning for sequential decision making or Bayesian experimental design

• Training models on multimodal scientific data such as text, images, spectra, or simulations

title: Salesforce Platform Developer
description:
Bright Vision Technologies is a forward-thinking software development company dedicated to building innovative solutions that help businesses automate and optimize their operations. We leverage cutting-edge technologies to create scalable, secure, and user-friendly applications.

As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a skilled Salesforce Platform Developer to join our dynamic team and contribute to our mission of transforming business processes through technology.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Salesforce Developer
Location: 100% Remote (Continental United States)
Position Type: In-house Bright Vision Technologies SOW engagement (no third-party client or vendor)
Salary : $100K - $150K
Experience: 5+ years

Employment Terms & Visa Policy
This is a 100% remote, full-time, direct W2 position with Bright Vision Technologies .
This role is part of Bright Vision Technologies ’ in-house Statement of Work (SOW) engagement. The client, end customer, and employer for this position is Bright Vision Technologies - there is no third-party client, vendor, or implementation partner involved.
We do not engage in C2C, 1099, or third-party arrangements for this role.

Candidates must be willing to work directly as a full-time W2 employee of Bright Vision Technologies and contribute to our in-house SOW deliverables.
No new H1B sponsorship is available for this role.

However, candidates who are currently on a valid H1B visa and require a transfer are welcome to apply. We will support H1B transfers for qualified candidates.
For every role, a technical coding assessment is mandatory. Please apply only if you are confident in your technical abilities and hands-on experience.

Job Summary
We are seeking a Salesforce Platform Developer to design and build production-grade Salesforce solutions using Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, and integration platforms. The role is deeply hands-on, with responsibility for delivering custom business logic, integrations, user interfaces, and automation that meet complex enterprise requirements while respecting platform limits and long-term maintainability. The ideal candidate has shipped meaningful Salesforce work in production, writes idiomatic Apex and modern LWC, and balances declarative-first thinking with the willingness to write code where it provides clear value.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop Apex classes, triggers, batch jobs, queueable jobs, and scheduled jobs that respect governor limits and bulkification principles.

• Build Lightning Web Components for rich, performant user experiences embedded across Salesforce surfaces.

• Design and implement automation using Flow, Process Builder migration, and declarative-first patterns.

• Develop integrations using REST, SOAP, Platform Events, Change Data Capture, and Salesforce Connect.

• Implement complex data models including custom objects, relationships, formula fields, and validation rules.

• Build and maintain sharing models, profiles, permission sets, and row-level security configurations.

• Develop and maintain comprehensive Apex unit tests with meaningful coverage and assertions.

• Implement CI/CD pipelines using Salesforce DX, Copado, Gearset, or AutoRABIT.

• Participate in code reviews, contribute to development standards, and document technical decisions.

• Troubleshoot production issues including governor-limit errors, integration failures, and data anomalies.

• Collaborate with admins, architects, and product owners to refine requirements.

• Optimize performance for large-data-volume scenarios, including selective queries and async patterns.

• Support upgrades, releases, and refactoring of legacy implementations toward modern patterns.

• Stay current with Salesforce releases, Einstein/Agentforce features, and platform innovations.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field.
